title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Analysis situs, 4th version, 1986). P is an ambient space (topological or stratified). M is a set of 'figures' X, each with a closed support |X| and an 'interior' or open stratum |X|°. The boundary is ∂X = |X| \ |X|° = ∪_{Z<X} |Z|°. Two orthogonality relations are used: Z |∘| X means |Z|° ∩ |X|° = ∅, and Z || X means |Z| ∩ |X| = ∅.

The combinatorial operators. For a family L ⊂ M:
- cosupp°(L) = {Z : Z |∘| Y for all Y ∈ L}.
- supp°(L) = cosupp°(cosupp°(L)), the double orthogonal.
This is the standard closure operator of the Galois connection (polarity) induced by the relation |∘|. The realization map φ sends a family A to φ(A) = ∪_{Y∈A} |Y|°.

Step 1. The previous page postulated a covering hypothesis: P \ |X| is covered by the |Z|° with Z orthogonal to X. Together with ∂X = ∪_{Z<X} |Z|° (faces satisfy Z |∘| X), this gives P \ |X|° = ∪_{Z∈cosupp°X} |Z|°. Grothendieck's NB: this alone does not exclude Z with |Z| ∩ |X|° ≠ ∅, since only the interiors are disjoint.

Step 2. Consequences:
- φ(cosupp° X) = P \ |X|°.
- φ(supp° X) = |X|°. Indeed, Y ∈ supp° X forces |Y|° to avoid every |Z|°, Z ∈ cosupp° X, hence |Y|° ⊂ |X|°; and X ∈ supp° X gives the reverse inclusion.

Step 3. Closed version. Let X̃ be the family of strata Y with |Y|° ⊂ |X| (X and its faces), so that |X| = ∪_{Y∈X̃} |Y|°. Define supp X = supp°(X̃) and cosupp X = cosupp°(X̃). Claim: φ(supp X) = |X| and φ(cosupp X) = P \ |X|.
- Easy inclusion: X̃ ⊂ supp X, so |X| ⊂ φ(supp X).
- Converse, by contraposition: suppose |Y|° ⊄ |X|, i.e. |Y|° ∩ (P \ |X|) ≠ ∅. One needs Z with Z |∘| X̃ (i.e. |Z|° ∩ |X| = ∅) and |Y|° ∩ |Z|° ≠ ∅, showing Y ∉ supp°(X̃). The page breaks off exactly here.
- The next page says this step needs the stronger hypothesis 'in all its force': P \ |X| is covered by interiors |Z|° of Z with |Z|° ∩ |X| = ∅. It then moves on to defining 'constructible internal supports' supp°(L) for families L majorized in a 'notion' F, and full faithfulness of the support functor X ↦ |X|.

Purpose. To recover topological subsets (open strata, closed supports, their complements) purely combinatorially from the orthogonality structure on the category of figures. This is part of a 'tame topology' / combinatorial analysis situs in which the geometric realization φ is compatible with the formal support operators.
errors: Last line of the transcription: the condition should read |X| ∩ |Z|° = ∅ (Z orthogonal to X̃), not ≠ ∅. The final '|Y|°∩|Z|°' is incomplete and should be '≠ ∅'.

The argument for φ(supp X) ⊂ |X| is not completed on this page. Under only the weak relation P\|X|° = ∪_{cosupp°X} |Z|° it does not follow: one needs the covering of P\|X| by interiors of Z with |Z|° ∩ |X| = ∅. Grothendieck acknowledges this on the next page; it is a gap, not an error.
The statement φ(cosupp X) = P \ |X| is asserted but not argued on this page. It requires the same strong covering hypothesis.

ideas.what: Supports defined as double orthogonals: supp°(L) = cosupp°(cosupp°(L)) for the 'disjoint interiors' relation, with realization φ(A) = union of open strata.
ideas.modern_name: Galois connection / polarity closure operator (cf. formal concept analysis; regular open algebra via double complement)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (polarities, 1940); Ore (Galois connections, 1944); Wille (formal concept analysis, 1982)
ideas.where_published: Not in published texts. Related 'tame topology' remarks appear in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), without this formalism.

ideas.what: Covering hypothesis: the complement of |X| is covered by interiors of figures orthogonal to X, ensuring φ(supp X) = |X| and φ(cosupp X) = P\|X|.
ideas.modern_name: Separation/covering axiom for a stratified or o-minimal-type structure ensuring the closure operator is 'spatial'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Analogues in o-minimal / stratification theory (van den Dries etc.); no exact standard name

ideas.what: Closed support of X as supp° of the family of its faces X̃, recovering |X| = ∪ of open faces.
ideas.modern_name: Closure of a cell as the union of its faces in a regular cell/stratified complex

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches an axiomatic recovery of the topology of a stratified space from an orthogonality relation on a category of figures, via Galois-closure 'supports'. This leads on the next page to 'constructible internal supports' and full faithfulness of the support functor. The program of characterising when such combinatorial supports match geometric ones does not seem developed in the tame-topology literature, though the ingredients are elementary.
missed.quote: Je dis qu'on a aussi φ(supp X) = |X|, φ(cosupp X) = P \ |X|
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Possible link between formal concept analysis/polarities and the combinatorial description of stratified or o-minimal spaces. It is of modest interest only.

deep.surprise_reason: An elementary Galois-connection argument inside a larger, unpublished axiomatics of 'analysis situs'. The individual steps are routine; only the overall program (tame topology via orthogonality of figures) is uncharted, and this page adds little to it.
transcription_corrections: 'On voit que se assure[?] déjà des deux relations' should read 'On voit qu'on s'assure déjà des deux relations' (probable).
'si [-...-] par définition' reads 'si par définition', with a struck word in between.
In 'i.e. |X| ∩ |Z|° ≠ ∅', the manuscript sense requires '= ∅'. The final '|Y|°∩|Z|°' is cut off and presumably continues '≠ ∅'.
'|Y|° ⊄ |X̃|' has a correction mark over the tilde; it means |Y|° ⊄ |X| (= ∪_{Y'∈X̃} |Y'|°).
'en raisonnant[?] dans le but[?]' is uncertain; possibly 'ou encore en raisonnant par contraposée'.
The '84' at the bottom left is the archive foliation number, not part of the text; '75' at top is Grothendieck's page number.
